scope: Real upstream Grim BadPacketsA triggers the unchanged example punishment command, links two historical accounts and one synthetic self-reported device, persists across normal server restart, rejects related re-entry, and restores access after explicit account/device unban. Isolated offline loopback TCP only.

examplePunishment.warning: Example thresholds are not recommendations from Grim authors. The template is an optional merge fragment; copying the complete fragment here is only for an empty QA fixture.

historicalFailures.observed: Both versions reached real BadPacketsA x120 and received the configured immediate Grim-BadPackets kick. The test incorrectly required the word banned; neither restart phase ran.
historicalFailures.fix: Only the trigger phase expects the exact configured immediate kick text; restart admission checks still require banned.

historicalFailures.observed: 1.20.1 passed both phases (12 groups); 1.21.1 passed trigger (6 groups) and exited 0, then Python probe.bind raised errno 98 before the restart JVM launched.
historicalFailures.inference: The immediate Linux bind failure after normal shutdown is consistent with TIME_WAIT socket state; kernel socket state was not captured, so TIME_WAIT is an inference.
historicalFailures.fix: POSIX probe sets SO_REUSEADDR then actually binds and listens; live-listener errors still fail. Windows does not set SO_REUSEADDR.

limits: One deterministic upstream BadPacketsA pattern does not measure overall cheating detection, evasion resistance, false positives, reach/movement coverage, or production performance.
Device identifiers and companion reports are synthetic client self-reports, not hardware attestation, genuine VM detection, or authenticated account ownership.
The historical associated account is offline during the trigger; immediate removal of an already-online associated account is not established by this specific run.
The complete default policy remains unchanged, but this suite does not exhaustively retest every IP quota or blacklist branch.
22-second clean admission precedes injected violations. This is not a new silent-client timeout measurement or graphical client test.
Only pinned Purpur/Grim pairs and released GPL Bukkit 0.1.1 were run here; other servers, mod loaders, proxies and later dependency versions need separate validation.
Offline loopback fixtures do not prove production account authentication or secure proxy forwarding.

privacyReview.note: Only explicit result/log/template files are copied. Four observed player UUIDs were independently matched to OfflinePlayer:<synthetic name>; no real player account or physical device identifier is present.
